episodes.title: Learning from different generations
episodes.description: When you were younger, did you have a special bond with your grandparents? Many of us develop particularly close attachments with older family members, but did you know that this ability for the oldest and youngest of our society to get along in a friendly way is not limited to families? In fact, there are some projects which pair together nurseries and retirement homes, to help reduce feelings of loneliness and improve everybody's general health and happiness. Georgie and Phil discuss this and…

episodes.title: Could vaccines cure cancer?
episodes.description: When was the last time you had a vaccination, and what was it for? Many of us get vaccinations when we are children or when we go travelling, but did you know that scientists have been developing vaccines that can be personalised to help your body keep itself clear of some specific cancer types? Georgie and Phil discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary. 6 Minute English now has a VIDEO VERSION! 6 Minute English now comes with a video! It's the same programme that you know and love, but no…

episodes.title: Is aircon the answer to a heating world?
episodes.description: Do you ever feel it is too hot to sleep? With climate change gradually increasing world temperatures, people across the world are becoming increasingly affected by hot weather. In many locations, air conditioning is used to help cool down homes and workplaces, but not everyone has access to this. And it isn't just about getting a good night's sleep – extremely hot weather can be a serious health risk. Georgie and Neil discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary. 6 Minute English now has a VI…

episodes.title: What should you eat for a better night’s sleep?
episodes.description: Have you ever had the feeling of lying awake at night, unable to get to sleep? Many of us know what it is like to struggle with sleep, especially if we have drunk too much tea or coffee before bed! But did you know that your sleep quality can be affected by other parts of your diet too? Georgie and Phil discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary. Get a free transcript and quiz at bbclearningenglish.com (currently experiencing technical issues). Sign up for our email newsletter for tips and…

episodes.title: Why has gold got so expensive?
episodes.description: Many of us own jewellery or other items that are gold coloured, but do you own anything that is made from real gold? Gold is a precious metal, which means that there is a limited supply in the world. This not only makes it expensive, but also means that it holds a relatively stable value. So, why are investors interested in it, and should the rest of us start buying more of it? Georgie and Phil discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary. 6 Minute English now has a VIDEO VERSION! 6 Minute En…

episodes.title: Are people drinking less alcohol?
episodes.description: In recent generations many people have chosen to stop drinking alcohol. Surveys from the UK suggest that 16 to 24-year-olds are more likely to be non-drinkers than the older generations. Many people are sharing their experience of drinking less alcohol or being completely sober on social media. Some people have been saying that they want to go out more to drink and have fun with friends, but they have concerns about fitness and wellness. Georgie and Neil discuss this and teach you some new voca…

episodes.title: Why does heartbreak hurt so much?
episodes.description: Anyone who has had their heart broken will know how horrible it feels. But did you know that the pain you feel is not just imaginary – it registers in the same part of the brain that processes physical pain. So, why do we feel this pain? And if it feels so bad, what is the point of being in love in the first place? Neil and Georgie discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary. 6 Minute English now has a VIDEO VERSION! 6 Minute English now comes with a video! It's the same programme that you k…

episodes.title: Why do we itch?
episodes.description: Feeling itchy is unpleasant, and the feeling of finally scratching that itch can be very satisfying! But why do we feel itchy in the first place? And is it possible to catch an itch from someone else? Neil and Georgie discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary. 6 Minute English now has a VIDEO VERSION! 6 Minute English now comes with a video! It's the same programme that you know and love, but now you can see us! Watch this podcast here (and find a free worksheet): https://www.bbc.co.uk/lea…

episodes.title: Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China
episodes.description: President Trump was greeted by President Xi Jinping at the airport as he arrived in Shenzhen for a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders, which will culminate in a closely-watched meeting on Thursday between the pair and the Russian president. In a highly choreographed moment, Trump and Xi shook hands on the tarmac. Later the US leader met Mr Putin ahead of a gala dinner. Also: Thousands of people in Haiti have marched in the capital in support of troops from El Salvador, who've been deployed to confr…

episodes.title: Nvidia rules out return for disgraced boss
episodes.description: Jensen Huang fails in his bid to be re-hired as CEO of Nvidia after a scandal over his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The US Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating whether the company misled investors. Nvidia has meanwhile reported a doubling of revenues during his last quarter in charge. Also: President Donald Trump is attending a regional economic summit in China, a day ahead of a historic meeting with his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, and the Russian leader, V…

episodes.title: Special episode: Trump, Putin and Xi meeting
episodes.description: This special episode of the Global News Podcast brings together our China specialist, our North America correspondent, and our Russia and Ukraine analyst, to discuss an unprecedented summit taking place this week. The US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping are due to meet in Shenzhen, China, for their first-ever trilateral talks. President Trump has said the agenda will include denuclearisation, the war with Iran, and the war in Ukraine. So…

episodes.title: Red carpet for Trump in Asia
episodes.description: In Manila the US president meets leaders of Japan, India and Australia - a grouping known as the Quad. He will head to China on Wednesday. Also: Ukrainian airstrikes cause extensive damage to bridge connecting occupied Crimea to Russia. UK announces sanctions on eight Israeli companies involved in building Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank. BBC World Service launches latest series of its education programme, for girls in Nigeria who cannot go to school. Panel of international judges…

episodes.title: OpenAI sued by California over rogue cyber attacks
episodes.description: The California Attorney General Rob Bonta is suing OpenAI, alleging the ChatGPT maker misled the public and put people at risk by developing AI models without adequate safeguards. The lawsuit cites the July 2026 attack on the AI platform Hugging Face, in which experimental OpenAI agents accessed the internet and breached the company's internal systems. An OpenAI spokesperson told the BBC that the lawsuit "appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that's been identified by every major AI lab…

episodes.title: Crimea Kerch Bridge hit in a huge Ukrainian drone attack
episodes.description: The Russian defence ministry says a record number of drones were fired from Ukraine overnight and more than 1300 were brought down by its air defences. An oil refinery in the Krasnodar region was targeted and there was damage to the Kerch Bridge which links Russia to occupied Crimea. Western countries call on Israel to allow rapid humanitarian access to Gaza. The Indonesian president apologises to neighbouring countries for the thick haze caused by massive forest fires in his country. The direc…

episodes.title: Government forces retreat in Yemen
episodes.description: Yemen's Saudi-backed government has been redeploying its forces to protect its temporary capital, Aden, after advances by the Houthi movement which is backed by Iran. They've withdrawn from an area overlooking the strategic Bab al-Mandeb Strait at the entrance to the Red Sea. It signalled the end of a six-week counter offensive to retake coastal territory from the Houthis, whose control over the Yemeni side of the Strait has further constrained Middle East oil exports. Also: the architect of Me…

episodes.title: The Global Story: How North Korea pulled off a $6bn heist
episodes.description: Last week saw what could be the biggest heist in history: $6.3bn was stolen from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance. North Korean hackers are suspected of being behind the attack, which saw billions of dollars disappear in just 20 minutes. It’s far from the first time North Korea has been accused of a major cyber-attack. Over the past decade, hackers linked to the country have targeted banks, public institutions and even Sony Pictures. On The Global Story, Asma Khalid speaks with journalist Ge…
